source_refs.note: Topic 14.2 with the Interesting Information box (PDF 21). The book's condition that the restoring force is 'proportional to the inertia of the body' is not a condition of S.H.M. and is not carried.

blocks.text: Simple harmonic motion is a type of oscillatory motion produced by a restoring force. For a body to execute simple harmonic motion:

items: The restoring force must be directly proportional to the displacement from the mean position.
The force and displacement follow Hooke's law, F = -kx, where k is the spring constant, which depends on the nature of the spring's material.
The acceleration must be proportional to the displacement, a proportional to -x; the negative sign shows that the acceleration is directed towards the mean position.

blocks.title: Interesting information
blocks.text: Not all periodic vibrations are simple harmonic, because not all restoring forces are proportional to the displacement. Any restoring force can cause oscillation. An electrocardiogram traces the periodic pattern of a beating heart, but the motion of its recorder needle is not simple harmonic, because the restoring force is not always proportional to the displacement from the mean position.

blocks.prompt: A body oscillates, but its acceleration is not proportional to its displacement. Is its motion simple harmonic?
blocks.explanation: No. It is oscillatory (periodic), but S.H.M. requires a = -(constant) x.

items: S.H.M.: restoring force proportional to displacement, F = -kx.
a proportional to -x: acceleration always towards the mean position.
Every S.H.M. is periodic, but not every periodic motion is S.H.M.
